Access is proposed via a new crossover from Old Coach Road, located approximately 140m from the intersection with Merindah–Maldon Road. The existing gravel farm gate will be removed. A secondary emergency access point will be provided to the north, connecting to the unmade road reserve (Crown Allotment 21, Parish of Merindah). This secondary access will be gated and locked, used only for emergency egress and maintenance.

**Building and Works Description**
The main building will be a single-storey, steel portal frame structure with insulated sandwich panel cladding (Colorbond finish, colour "Surfmist"). Total building footprint is 18,450m², with a maximum ridge height of 12.5m. The building is divided into three functional areas:

1. **Freezer hall** – 9,800m², operating at -22°C. Equipped with high-bay racking (9 levels) and a mezzanine level for picking operations.
2. **Chiller hall** – 6,200m², operating at +2°C. Includes a dedicated produce ripening room (1,200m²) with ethylene gas management.
3. **Ancillary areas** – 2,450m² including loading docks, battery charging room, workshop, and staff amenities.

The facility will operate 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, with peak staffing of 45 full-time equivalent staff (day shift) and 12 staff (night shift). Deliveries and dispatch are proposed between 5:00am and 10:00pm Monday to Saturday, with limited Sunday operations (6:00am–12:00pm) for temperature-sensitive freight only.

**Planned Capacity**
The facility is designed to accommodate a planned_capacity_pallet_spaces of 12000 pallets across the freezer and chiller halls combined. This capacity is based on Australian standard pallet dimensions (1165mm x 1165mm) and includes provision for both bulk storage and racked pallet positions. The racking layout has been optimised to allow for future expansion of up to 15% capacity within the existing building envelope without requiring additional floor area.

In the planning application, ColdChain Logistics states that the Gawler River Cold Storage Facility will have a planned_capacity_pallet_spaces of 12000 pallets. Record status: current. This figure is current and represents the operational design capacity at full build-out. The capacity calculation is provided in the accompanying Pallet Flow Analysis (Attachment C, prepared by Logistics Design Associates, dated 18 December 2024).

**Traffic and Access**
A Traffic Impact Assessment (Attachment D) has been prepared by Traffix Group. Key findings include:
- Predicted daily vehicle movements: 320 light vehicles and 180 heavy vehicles (articulated and rigid trucks)
- Peak hour movements: 45 vehicle movements (AM) and 38 (PM)
- The existing Old Coach Road pavement has adequate capacity; however, the applicant proposes to contribute to the upgrade of the intersection at Old Coach Road / Merindah–Maldon Road (left-turn lane on the eastern approach) as part of a Section 173 Agreement.

The truck holding yard will accommodate up to 8 semi-trailers waiting for dock assignment. Queuing on the public road will not occur as the internal holding area has been sized to absorb peak arrival rates.

**Stormwater and Environment**
Stormwater will be collected via a network of pits and pipes and treated through a 1,200m³ bio-retention basin before discharge to the existing drainage line at the north-east corner. A Sediment and Erosion Control Plan will be implemented during construction in accordance with EPA Publication 275. No groundwater extraction is proposed. The facility will use an ammonia-based refrigeration system (low-GWP refrigerant) with a closed-loop glycol secondary circuit.

Waste management: organic waste from produce handling will be stored in a sealed, refrigerated skip and collected twice weekly. All other waste will be compacted and removed by licensed contractors.

- Noise management, in accordance with EPA guidelines.
- Erosion and sediment control, including the installation of silt fences and sediment basins.

**5.2 Traffic Impact and Access Arrangements**

The proposed development will generate a relatively modest volume of traffic when compared to the existing daily movements along Gawler River Road and Old Coach Road. The facility is intended to operate on a continuous basis, with cold storage requiring consistent temperature management; however, the majority of staff movements will occur during standard business hours, with a reduced night shift for monitoring and maintenance.

**Access Points**

The site will be accessed via a single new crossover from Old Coach Road, located approximately 120 metres south of the intersection with Gawler River Road. The crossover has been designed to accommodate the swept path of a 19-metre semi-trailer and will provide a width of 8.0 metres at the property boundary, flaring to 12.5 metres within the site to allow for comfortable entry and exit movements.

A secondary access point, intended for emergency vehicles and maintenance personnel only, is proposed along the western boundary of the site. This access will not be available for general staff or delivery vehicles and will be secured with a locked gate. The emergency access will connect to an unsealed track that runs parallel to the western boundary, which is currently used for agricultural purposes.

No direct access is proposed from Gawler River Road. Vehicles entering or exiting the site will be required to utilise Old Coach Road in a northbound or southbound direction, with the crossover positioned to provide adequate sight distance in both directions. A swept path analysis has been prepared and is included as Attachment 6 to this application.

- Staff parking: 28 spaces, including 2 accessible spaces and 4 spaces designated for electric vehicle charging.
- Visitor parking: 6 spaces located adjacent to the office entry.
- Loading and unloading: 8 dedicated dock positions, with an additional 4 hardstand areas for queuing of heavy vehicles.
- Bicycle parking: 10 hoops (20 bike positions) located under the main awning near the staff entry.

The car park will be constructed with a two-coat bitumen seal, with line marking and signage provided in accordance with Australian Standard AS 2890.1. A landscape buffer of approximately 3 metres will be provided between the car park and the northern boundary, incorporating a mix of native shrubs and groundcover species.

The facility is anticipated to receive an average of 24 heavy vehicle movements per day (12 arrivals and 12 departures) during peak operations. These movements will predominantly occur between 5:00 am and 8:00 pm, with occasional deliveries outside these hours for temperature-sensitive product. The majority of heavy vehicles will be semi-trailers, with a smaller number of B-double movements (estimated at no more than 4 per day) utilising the Gawler River Road corridor.

Truck routeing will be restricted to the following:

- From the north (Sturt Highway / Gawler Bypass): via Gawler River Road to Old Coach Road.
- From the south (Port Wakefield Road): via Gawler River Road to Old Coach Road.
- From the east (Horrocks Highway): via Gawler River Road to Old Coach Road.

Trucks will not be permitted to use local residential streets, including Shepherdson Road, Mibus Court, or the eastern end of Gawler River Road beyond the site frontage. A truck routeing plan is provided as Attachment 7.

ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT PLAN SUMMARY

This section of the application summarises the environmental management measures proposed for the construction and ongoing operation of the Gawler River Cold Storage Facility. The full Environmental Management Plan (EMP) is provided as Attachment 8 to this application. The EMP has been prepared in accordance with the Environment Protection Authority (EPA) guidelines for warehouse and logistics facilities and addresses the following key aspects:

**Waste Management**

General waste generated during the construction phase will comprise packaging materials, off-cuts of building materials, and limited domestic-type waste from site workers. All construction waste will be segregated on site into the following streams:

- Clean fill and excavated material (reused on site where practicable)
- Concrete and masonry (crushed and reused as site fill or removed by a licensed contractor)
- Timber and packaging (recycled where possible)
- General waste (collected in covered skip bins and disposed of at the Gawler River Transfer Station)

A minimum of 80% (by weight) of construction waste is targeted for recycling or reuse. The construction contractor will be required to maintain waste dockets and provide a waste summary report to the applicant at practical completion.

Operational waste from the facility will include:

- Cardboard and paper packaging from incoming and outgoing goods
- Plastic film and pallet wrap
- Wooden pallets (repaired and reused on site or returned to suppliers)
- Damaged or expired product (including temperature-compromised foodstuffs)
- General office and staff amenity waste
- Scrap metal from maintenance activities
- Waste cooking oil from the staff canteen (collected by a licensed recycler)

Cardboard will be baled on site using a compacting baler located in the waste storage area to the north-east of the loading dock. Baled cardboard will be collected fortnightly by a commercial recycling contractor. Plastic film will be similarly baled and collected. General waste will be collected three times per week.

The waste storage area will be a covered, hardstand enclosure with a concrete floor, bunded to contain any liquid spillage. The enclosure will be screened from view by a 2.4 metre colourbond fence and will be secured with a lockable gate. Bins will be clearly labelled and maintained in good condition to prevent litter and vermin access.

Temperature-compromised product will be held in a dedicated quarantine bin within the waste enclosure and collected within 48 hours by a licensed waste contractor for disposal at an approved facility. The applicant will maintain a register of all waste disposals, including the waste type, quantity, date of collection, and the name of the receiving facility.

**Stormwater Management**

The site is located within the Gawler River catchment. The existing land use is a disused agricultural paddock with limited impervious surfaces. The development will introduce approximately 2.1 hectares of impervious area (building footprint, hardstand, car parking, and access roads).

Stormwater management has been designed to comply with the requirements of the Gawler River Council Development Plan and the EPA Stormwater Pollution Prevention Code of Practice. The key principles of the design are:
**DA-2025-001 – Gawler River Cold Storage Facility**
**Section 5 – Building Design and Construction**

**5.1 Building Layout and Massing**

The proposed building is a single-storey, rectangular cold storage facility with a total gross floor area of approximately 8,450 m². The building footprint is 132 m (north-south) by 64 m (east-west), positioned centrally within the subject land to maximise separation from the northern and eastern boundaries. The main structure comprises three distinct functional zones:

- **Zone A – Freezer storage:** 4,200 m², operating at -22°C to -25°C
- **Zone B – Chiller storage:** 2,900 m², operating at 0°C to 4°C
- **Zone C – Receival, dispatch, and support areas:** 1,350 m², including the loading dock, office, staff amenities, plant room, and battery charging area

The building height to the ridge of the gable roof is 12.6 m at its highest point. The roof is a low-pitch (5-degree) gable design with a pre-painted Colorbond steel cladding in the colour "Zincalume" (finish: standard matt). The roof sheeting is insulated with a 100 mm closed-cell polyisocyanurate (PIR) foam core, laminated between two layers of 0.42 mm steel, providing a combined system R-value of 5.6 m²·K/W. The roof is designed to accommodate a future photovoltaic array; structural provisions for the additional dead load have been included in the frame design.

The external walls are constructed from pre-cast concrete panels, 180 mm thick, with a smooth off-form finish. The panels are sealed with a vapour-permeable membrane on the exterior face and a vapour barrier on the interior face to prevent condensation and interstitial moisture. The wall system provides a thermal resistance of R 3.2 m²·K/W. All external wall penetrations (for refrigeration line sets, electrical conduits, and ventilation) will be sealed with a fire-rated, vapour-tight mastic.

**5.2 Floor Construction and Insulation**

The floor slab is a 200 mm thick reinforced concrete slab on grade, designed to support a uniformly distributed live load of 15 kPa and a point load of 40 kN from forklift wheels. The slab is cast on a 150 mm compacted crushed rock base, over a 0.2 mm high-density polyethylene vapour barrier. A 150 mm layer of extruded polystyrene (XPS) insulation is placed beneath the slab in the freezer and chiller zones to limit heat gain and prevent frost heave. The insulation has a compressive strength of 400 kPa and a thermal resistance of R 5.0 m²·K/W.

The slab in the freezer zone is equipped with a hydronic under-slab heating system to prevent soil freezing beneath the insulation. The system circulates a 30% propylene glycol solution at 5°C through 20 mm PEX piping embedded in the slab. The heating system is powered by a dedicated heat pump that also serves the office heating loop in winter. The system is controlled by a thermostat set to maintain slab temperature at 3°C ± 1°C.

**5.3 Refrigeration System Integration**

The refrigeration system is a centralised, two-stage ammonia (R-717) system with a design cooling capacity of 1,200 kW for the freezer zone and 640 kW for the chiller zone. The system uses four screw compressors (two duty, two standby) located in a dedicated plant room on the south-east corner of the building. The plant room is a separate fire-rated enclosure with a minimum 120-minute fire resistance level (FRL), ventilated to the outside with a mechanical exhaust system sized for the ammonia detection system.

*Question 1 – Truck movements and hours of operation.*
Several attendees asked about the number of truck movements expected per day and the hours during which deliveries would be accepted. The applicant confirmed that the facility would operate on a 24-hour basis for the refrigeration plant, but that truck movements would be restricted to the hours of 6:00 am to 10:00 pm, Monday to Saturday. The expected average is 12 heavy vehicle movements per day, with a peak of 18 movements during the harvest season (November to February).

*Question 3 – Stormwater and drainage.*
A question was raised regarding the potential for stormwater runoff from the large roof area to affect the Gawler River, which is approximately 800 m south of the site. The project engineer explained that the stormwater management plan provides for on-site detention with a discharge rate limited to the pre-development flow for the 1 in 100 year event. A sediment basin will be constructed during the construction phase, and the final landscaping plan includes a vegetated swale along the western boundary.

**1. INTRODUCTION**

This assessment was undertaken in accordance with the Merindah Council’s obligations under the Food Act 2001 (SA) and the Public Health Act 2011 (SA). The purpose of the assessment is to determine the food safety and sanitation requirements for the Gawler River Cold Storage Facility, which operates as a multi-temperature warehousing and distribution hub for fresh produce, dairy, and frozen goods.

The facility commenced operations in January 2025 and was brought to the attention of the EH Unit following a routine complaint regarding drainage from the loading dock. Since that initial contact, the facility has been inspected on three occasions and has cooperated with all requests for information. This document forms the first part of the overall assessment and addresses the food safety licensing requirements. A separate assessment covering waste management and pest control will be issued under separate cover.

**2. LICENSING REQUIREMENTS – FINDINGS**

The following findings relate to the food safety licensing status and requirements for the facility. These findings are based on inspections conducted on 18 February 2025, 14 May 2025, and 22 August 2025, as well as a review of documentation provided by the operator.

**Finding 1 – Food Safety License Required**

The Merindah Environmental Health Unit assessment notes that the food_safety_license_required for the facility is primary_producer_license. Record status: pending verification. This determination was made on the basis of the facility’s operational profile, which primarily involves the storage and distribution of unprocessed or minimally processed primary produce (including whole fruit, vegetables, and eggs) on behalf of third-party growers.

The licence type is recorded as a current entry in the Council’s food business register as at 1 September 2025. The operator was formally notified of this requirement by letter dated 28 February 2025 (ref: EH/LIC/2025/087), and has been operating under the terms of that licence since 1 April 2025.

**Finding 2 – Scope of Licence**

The primary producer licence applies to the storage and transport of whole, unprocessed primary produce only. It does not extend to activities involving the cutting, peeling, or further processing of produce, nor to the handling of ready-to-eat foods. During the inspection of 14 May 2025, it was confirmed that the facility does not undertake any such activities on site. All produce received is in its original field packaging or in bulk bins, and is dispatched in the same form.

**Finding 3 – Conditions of Licence**

The following conditions are attached to the primary producer licence held by the facility:

- Temperature logs must be maintained for all cold rooms and freezer units, and retained for a minimum of 12 months.
- All produce storage areas must be kept clean and free of accumulated debris.
- Pest control measures must be in place and documented, in accordance with the facility’s approved pest management plan.
- Training records for all staff handling produce must be kept up to date and available for inspection.

These conditions are consistent with the facility’s current operational practices as observed during inspections.

**Section 5 – Waste Management and Hygiene Practices**
**Merindah Environmental Health Unit**

**5.1 Overview**

This section of the assessment addresses waste disposal arrangements, general hygiene practices, and the management of potential public health impacts associated with waste handling at the Gawler River Cold Storage Facility. The facility operates a cold-chain logistics business storing whole primary produce (fruit, vegetables, eggs) on behalf of third-party growers, as described in the preceding sections of this assessment.

Waste streams generated by the facility are limited in type and volume, but require specific management controls due to the risk of attracting pests, creating odours, or contaminating stored produce. The waste streams identified during the assessment are:

- Organic waste (spoiled or damaged produce, field debris, packing material)
- Cardboard and paper packaging
- Plastic film and strapping
- General refuse (office waste, staff meal remnants)
- Wastewater from cleaning operations (cold room washdowns, equipment cleaning)

No hazardous waste streams were identified. The facility does not undertake processing activities that would generate chemical or biological waste beyond these categories.

---

**5.2 Inspection Findings**

Inspections relevant to waste management were conducted on the following dates:

- 14 May 2025 (full facility inspection)
- 23 July 2025 (follow-up waste management inspection)
- 19 August 2025 (spot check – waste storage area and bin washdown)

The 14 May inspection confirmed that waste accumulation in the produce storage areas was minimal. However, the follow-up inspection on 23 July identified a number of issues in the external waste storage area that required corrective action. These are detailed below.

---

**5.3 Waste Storage and Collection Arrangements**

The facility contracts with Merindah Regional Waste Services for general waste collection (240L bins, collected twice weekly) and with Gawler River Recycling Co. for cardboard and plastic recycling (collected weekly). Organic produce waste is collected by a separate contractor, Valley Organics Recovery, on an as-needed basis, typically every 5–7 days during peak season.

The external waste storage area is located on the eastern boundary of the facility, approximately 30 metres from the main cold room entrance. It is a covered, concrete-floored enclosure with a lockable gate. The enclosure is shared with the neighbouring packing shed, and the shared access arrangement is noted in the site lease.

**Finding 4 – Waste Storage Area Condition (23 July 2025)**

During the 23 July inspection, the following issues were recorded:

- Overflowing organic waste bins – two 240L bins were overfilled, with spoiled produce (tomatoes, leafy greens) spilling onto the concrete floor.
- Odour – a noticeable putrid odour was present in the enclosure and detectable approximately 10 metres downwind.
- Pest activity – evidence of rodent activity (droppings, gnaw marks on bin lids) was observed in the enclosure.
- Bin cleanliness – bins showed visible residue build-up on the interior surfaces, particularly the organic waste bins.

The operator was directed to undertake the following corrective actions within 7 days:

1. Remove all waste from the enclosure and arrange for an additional collection.
2. Clean and disinfect the enclosure floor and all bins.
3. Contact the pest control contractor (Ace Pest Management, under the facility’s approved pest management plan) to inspect the enclosure and surrounding area.
4. Review the organic waste collection schedule and increase frequency if required.

**6. Overall Compliance Summary**

The Gawler River Cold Storage Facility has been subject to environmental health assessment across the period February to September 2025, comprising two scheduled inspections, one follow-up inspection, and a review of operational documentation including temperature logs, pest control reports, and waste disposal contracts.

The facility operates under Food Act 1984 (Vic) registration and is classified as a high-risk food premises due to the scale of cold storage and handling of fresh produce. No further enforcement action is proposed at this time. **6.2 Findings from the Follow-Up Inspection (24 September 2025)**

A follow-up inspection was conducted on 24 September 2025 to verify that the corrective actions directed on 23 July 2025 had been completed. The inspection was attended by the facility manager and the environmental health officer.

This Department does not issue a general licence or certificate that covers all exports. Access is proposed via a new crossover from Old Coach Road, located approximately 140m from the intersection with Merindah–Maldon Road. The existing gravel farm gate will be removed. A secondary emergency access point will be provided to the north, connecting to the unmade road reserve (Crown Allotment 21, Parish of Merindah). This secondary access will be gated and locked, used only for emergency egress and maintenance.

**Building and Works Description**
The main building will be a single-storey, steel portal frame structure with insulated sandwich panel cladding (Colorbond finish, colour "Surfmist"). Total building footprint is 18,450m², with a maximum ridge height of 12.5m. The building is divided into three functional areas:

1. **Freezer hall** – 9,800m², operating at -22°C. Equipped with high-bay racking (9 levels) and a mezzanine level for picking operations.
2. **Chiller hall** – 6,200m², operating at +2°C. Includes a dedicated produce ripening room (1,200m²) with ethylene gas management.
3. **Ancillary areas** – 2,450m² including loading docks, battery charging room, workshop, and staff amenities.

The facility will operate 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, with peak staffing of 45 full-time equivalent staff (day shift) and 12 staff (night shift). Deliveries and dispatch are proposed between 5:00am and 10:00pm Monday to Saturday, with limited Sunday operations (6:00am–12:00pm) for temperature-sensitive freight only.

**Planned Capacity**
The facility is designed to accommodate a planned_capacity_pallet_spaces of 12000 pallets across the freezer and chiller halls combined. This capacity is based on Australian standard pallet dimensions (1165mm x 1165mm) and includes provision for both bulk storage and racked pallet positions. The racking layout has been optimised to allow for future expansion of up to 15% capacity within the existing building envelope without requiring additional floor area.

In the planning application, ColdChain Logistics states that the Gawler River Cold Storage Facility will have a planned_capacity_pallet_spaces of 12000 pallets. Record status: current. This figure is current and represents the operational design capacity at full build-out. The capacity calculation is provided in the accompanying Pallet Flow Analysis (Attachment C, prepared by Logistics Design Associates, dated 18 December 2024).

**Traffic and Access**
A Traffic Impact Assessment (Attachment D) has been prepared by Traffix Group. Key findings include:
- Predicted daily vehicle movements: 320 light vehicles and 180 heavy vehicles (articulated and rigid trucks)
- Peak hour movements: 45 vehicle movements (AM) and 38 (PM)
- The existing Old Coach Road pavement has adequate capacity; however, the applicant proposes to contribute to the upgrade of the intersection at Old Coach Road / Merindah–Maldon Road (left-turn lane on the eastern approach) as part of a Section 173 Agreement.

The truck holding yard will accommodate up to 8 semi-trailers waiting for dock assignment. Queuing on the public road will not occur as the internal holding area has been sized to absorb peak arrival rates.

**Stormwater and Environment**
Stormwater will be collected via a network of pits and pipes and treated through a 1,200m³ bio-retention basin before discharge to the existing drainage line at the north-east corner. A Sediment and Erosion Control Plan will be implemented during construction in accordance with EPA Publication 275. No groundwater extraction is proposed. The facility will use an ammonia-based refrigeration system (low-GWP refrigerant) with a closed-loop glycol secondary circuit.

Waste management: organic waste from produce handling will be stored in a sealed, refrigerated skip and collected twice weekly. All other waste will be compacted and removed by licensed contractors.

**5.2 Traffic Impact and Access Arrangements**

A secondary access point, intended for emergency vehicles and maintenance personnel only, is proposed along the western boundary of the site. This access will not be available for general staff or delivery vehicles and will be secured with a locked gate. The emergency access will connect to an unsealed track that runs parallel to the western boundary, which is currently used for agricultural purposes.

No direct access is proposed from Gawler River Road. Vehicles entering or exiting the site will be required to utilise Old Coach Road in a northbound or southbound direction, with the crossover positioned to provide adequate sight distance in both directions. A swept path analysis has been prepared and is included as Attachment 6 to this application.

**Car Parking**

The following car parking provision is proposed:

- Staff parking: 28 spaces, including 2 accessible spaces and 4 spaces designated for electric vehicle charging.
- Visitor parking: 6 spaces located adjacent to the office entry.
- Loading and unloading: 8 dedicated dock positions, with an additional 4 hardstand areas for queuing of heavy vehicles.
- Bicycle parking: 10 hoops (20 bike positions) located under the main awning near the staff entry.

**Heavy Vehicle Movements**

The facility is anticipated to receive an average of 24 heavy vehicle movements per day (12 arrivals and 12 departures) during peak operations. These movements will predominantly occur between 5:00 am and 8:00 pm, with occasional deliveries outside these hours for temperature-sensitive product. The majority of heavy vehicles will be semi-trailers, with a smaller number of B-double movements (estimated at no more than 4 per day) utilising the Gawler River Road corridor.

- From the south (Port Wakefield Road): via Gawler River Road to Old Coach Road.
- From the east (Horrocks Highway): via Gawler River Road to Old Coach Road.

Trucks will not be permitted to use local residential streets, including Shepherdson Road, Mibus Court, or the eastern end of Gawler River Road beyond the site frontage. A truck routeing plan is provided as Attachment 7.

**DA-2025-001 – Gawler River Cold Storage Facility**
**Section 5 – Building Design and Construction**

**5.1 Building Layout and Massing**

The proposed building is a single-storey, rectangular cold storage facility with a total gross floor area of approximately 8,450 m². The building footprint is 132 m (north-south) by 64 m (east-west), positioned centrally within the subject land to maximise separation from the northern and eastern boundaries. The main structure comprises three distinct functional zones:

- **Zone A – Freezer storage:** 4,200 m², operating at -22°C to -25°C
- **Zone B – Chiller storage:** 2,900 m², operating at 0°C to 4°C
- **Zone C – Receival, dispatch, and support areas:** 1,350 m², including the loading dock, office, staff amenities, plant room, and battery charging area

The building height to the ridge of the gable roof is 12.6 m at its highest point. The roof is a low-pitch (5-degree) gable design with a pre-painted Colorbond steel cladding in the colour "Zincalume" (finish: standard matt). The roof sheeting is insulated with a 100 mm closed-cell polyisocyanurate (PIR) foam core, laminated between two layers of 0.42 mm steel, providing a combined system R-value of 5.6 m²·K/W. The roof is designed to accommodate a future photovoltaic array; structural provisions for the additional dead load have been included in the frame design.

The external walls are constructed from pre-cast concrete panels, 180 mm thick, with a smooth off-form finish. The panels are sealed with a vapour-permeable membrane on the exterior face and a vapour barrier on the interior face to prevent condensation and interstitial moisture. The wall system provides a thermal resistance of R 3.2 m²·K/W. All external wall penetrations (for refrigeration line sets, electrical conduits, and ventilation) will be sealed with a fire-rated, vapour-tight mastic.

**5.2 Floor Construction and Insulation**

The floor slab is a 200 mm thick reinforced concrete slab on grade, designed to support a uniformly distributed live load of 15 kPa and a point load of 40 kN from forklift wheels. The slab is cast on a 150 mm compacted crushed rock base, over a 0.2 mm high-density polyethylene vapour barrier. A 150 mm layer of extruded polystyrene (XPS) insulation is placed beneath the slab in the freezer and chiller zones to limit heat gain and prevent frost heave. The insulation has a compressive strength of 400 kPa and a thermal resistance of R 5.0 m²·K/W.

The slab in the freezer zone is equipped with a hydronic under-slab heating system to prevent soil freezing beneath the insulation. The system circulates a 30% propylene glycol solution at 5°C through 20 mm PEX piping embedded in the slab. The heating system is powered by a dedicated heat pump that also serves the office heating loop in winter. The system is controlled by a thermostat set to maintain slab temperature at 3°C ± 1°C.

**5.3 Refrigeration System Integration**

The refrigeration system is a centralised, two-stage ammonia (R-717) system with a design cooling capacity of 1,200 kW for the freezer zone and 640 kW for the chiller zone. The system uses four screw compressors (two duty, two standby) located in a dedicated plant room on the south-east corner of the building. The plant room is a separate fire-rated enclosure with a minimum 120-minute fire resistance level (FRL), ventilated to the outside with a mechanical exhaust system sized for the ammonia detection system.

**1. INTRODUCTION**

This assessment was undertaken in accordance with the Merindah Council’s obligations under the Food Act 2001 (SA) and the Public Health Act 2011 (SA). The purpose of the assessment is to determine the food safety and sanitation requirements for the Gawler River Cold Storage Facility, which operates as a multi-temperature warehousing and distribution hub for fresh produce, dairy, and frozen goods.

The facility commenced operations in January 2025 and was brought to the attention of the EH Unit following a routine complaint regarding drainage from the loading dock. Since that initial contact, the facility has been inspected on three occasions and has cooperated with all requests for information. This document forms the first part of the overall assessment and addresses the food safety licensing requirements. A separate assessment covering waste management and pest control will be issued under separate cover.

**2. LICENSING REQUIREMENTS – FINDINGS**

The following findings relate to the food safety licensing status and requirements for the facility. These findings are based on inspections conducted on 18 February 2025, 14 May 2025, and 22 August 2025, as well as a review of documentation provided by the operator.

**Finding 1 – Food Safety License Required**

The Merindah Environmental Health Unit assessment notes that the food_safety_license_required for the facility is primary_producer_license. Record status: pending verification. This determination was made on the basis of the facility’s operational profile, which primarily involves the storage and distribution of unprocessed or minimally processed primary produce (including whole fruit, vegetables, and eggs) on behalf of third-party growers.

The licence type is recorded as a current entry in the Council’s food business register as at 1 September 2025. The operator was formally notified of this requirement by letter dated 28 February 2025 (ref: EH/LIC/2025/087), and has been operating under the terms of that licence since 1 April 2025.

**Finding 2 – Scope of Licence**

The primary producer licence applies to the storage and transport of whole, unprocessed primary produce only. It does not extend to activities involving the cutting, peeling, or further processing of produce, nor to the handling of ready-to-eat foods. During the inspection of 14 May 2025, it was confirmed that the facility does not undertake any such activities on site. All produce received is in its original field packaging or in bulk bins, and is dispatched in the same form.

**Finding 3 – Conditions of Licence**

The following conditions are attached to the primary producer licence held by the facility:

- Temperature logs must be maintained for all cold rooms and freezer units, and retained for a minimum of 12 months.
- All produce storage areas must be kept clean and free of accumulated debris.
- Pest control measures must be in place and documented, in accordance with the facility’s approved pest management plan.
- Training records for all staff handling produce must be kept up to date and available for inspection.

These conditions are consistent with the facility’s current operational practices as observed during inspections.

**Environmental Health Assessment – Gawler River Cold Storage Facility**
**Section 5 – Waste Management and Hygiene Practices**
**Merindah Environmental Health Unit**
**Assessment period: February – September 2025**

---

**5.1 Overview**

This section of the assessment addresses waste disposal arrangements, general hygiene practices, and the management of potential public health impacts associated with waste handling at the Gawler River Cold Storage Facility. The facility operates a cold-chain logistics business storing whole primary produce (fruit, vegetables, eggs) on behalf of third-party growers, as described in the preceding sections of this assessment.

Waste streams generated by the facility are limited in type and volume, but require specific management controls due to the risk of attracting pests, creating odours, or contaminating stored produce. The waste streams identified during the assessment are:

- Organic waste (spoiled or damaged produce, field debris, packing material)
- Cardboard and paper packaging
- Plastic film and strapping
- General refuse (office waste, staff meal remnants)
- Wastewater from cleaning operations (cold room washdowns, equipment cleaning)

No hazardous waste streams were identified. The facility does not undertake processing activities that would generate chemical or biological waste beyond these categories.

---

**5.2 Inspection Findings**

Inspections relevant to waste management were conducted on the following dates:

- 14 May 2025 (full facility inspection)
- 23 July 2025 (follow-up waste management inspection)
- 19 August 2025 (spot check – waste storage area and bin washdown)

The 14 May inspection confirmed that waste accumulation in the produce storage areas was minimal. However, the follow-up inspection on 23 July identified a number of issues in the external waste storage area that required corrective action. These are detailed below.

---

**5.3 Waste Storage and Collection Arrangements**

The facility contracts with Merindah Regional Waste Services for general waste collection (240L bins, collected twice weekly) and with Gawler River Recycling Co. for cardboard and plastic recycling (collected weekly). Organic produce waste is collected by a separate contractor, Valley Organics Recovery, on an as-needed basis, typically every 5–7 days during peak season.

The external waste storage area is located on the eastern boundary of the facility, approximately 30 metres from the main cold room entrance. It is a covered, concrete-floored enclosure with a lockable gate. The enclosure is shared with the neighbouring packing shed, and the shared access arrangement is noted in the site lease.

**Finding 4 – Waste Storage Area Condition (23 July 2025)**

During the 23 July inspection, the following issues were recorded:

- Overflowing organic waste bins – two 240L bins were overfilled, with spoiled produce (tomatoes, leafy greens) spilling onto the concrete floor.
- Odour – a noticeable putrid odour was present in the enclosure and detectable approximately 10 metres downwind.
- Pest activity – evidence of rodent activity (droppings, gnaw marks on bin lids) was observed in the enclosure.
- Bin cleanliness – bins showed visible residue build-up on the interior surfaces, particularly the organic waste bins.

The operator was directed to undertake the following corrective actions within 7 days:

1. Remove all waste from the enclosure and arrange for an additional collection.
2. Clean and disinfect the enclosure floor and all bins.
3. Contact the pest control contractor (Ace Pest Management, under the facility’s approved pest management plan) to inspect the enclosure and surrounding area.
4. Review the organic waste collection schedule and increase frequency if required.

14 Borthwick Avenue

**RE: Clarification of export requirements for temperature-controlled storage facility – Wingfield**

Dear Ms. Nguyen,

Thank you for your email of 27 February 2026 and for the subsequent telephone discussion with our officer Mr. D. Kowalski on 6 March 2026. This letter responds to your questions about whether your facility requires export approval from this Department for the goods you handle, and about the steps you should take if your client base expands to include overseas markets.

I understand from our conversation that Adelaide Cold Chain Logistics operates a multi-temperature warehouse at the Wingfield address, providing blast freezing, chilled storage, and frozen storage for a range of food products destined for both the domestic retail and food service sectors. You also mentioned that one of your larger clients has been approached by an exporter in Singapore, and you wanted to know whether that enquiry changes your current obligations.

**Summary of your current status**

In correspondence, the Department of Primary Industries and Regions states that the export_approval_status is not_applied. Record status: current. This is correct for your current operations as described. Please note that this status applies to the facility at Wingfield only, and it is not a reflection on the suitability or otherwise of your premises or your food safety management systems.

**What "not applied" means in practice**

This Department does not issue a general licence or certificate that covers all exports. Export approval is product- and market-specific, and it is usually sought by the manufacturer or the principal exporter of the goods, not by a third-party storage provider. The fact that you have not applied for, and do not hold, an export approval from PIRSA is consistent with the nature of your current business as a contract storage and logistics provider.

There are, however, two situations in which your facility may need to become part of an export approval arrangement:

1. **The exporter holds an existing arrangement.** If your client's Singapore enquiry leads to a formal export order, the exporter should contact the relevant authority in their own supply chain first. For many processed foods, the exporting manufacturer will hold an export registration with the Commonwealth Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF) or with this Department under a delegated arrangement. That registration may list approved storage facilities. If your Wingfield site is not already listed on the exporter's registration, the exporter can apply to have it added, and our officers may then need to inspect the facility to confirm it meets the relevant cold chain requirements.

2. **You become the exporter of record.** If Adelaide Cold Chain Logistics were to purchase product and sell it overseas in your own name, you would then be the exporter and would need to hold the necessary export documentation. In that case, you should contact us before you commit to any overseas order so we can advise on the specific commodity requirements.

**What you do not need to do now**

You do not need to submit an application for export approval at this stage. You also do not need to register with us as a food business, because your existing domestic food safety registration with the City of Port Adelaide Enfield council covers the handling of the products while they are in your care. I have copied the relevant section of the *Food Act 2001* (SA) guidance below for your reference, but the short version is that a storage facility that does not itself sell food to the public is not required to hold a separate PIRSA registration.

I refer to our telephone conversation on 15 October 2026 and to the site inspection of your Wingfield facility conducted by Ms T. Nguyen (Senior Food Safety Officer) on 22 September 2026. Thank you for accommodating that inspection at short notice, and for providing the temperature mapping records for the freezer and chiller bays.

This letter confirms the advice given verbally and provides further guidance on the matters you raised regarding a potential export order to Singapore. I understand from our conversation that a prospective buyer has asked whether your facility holds any export approvals, and you are seeking clarity on what, if anything, you need to do.

**Summary of the current position**

As outlined in my previous letter of 2 October 2026, your facility does not currently require an export approval from this Department. Your business operates as a contract storage and logistics provider, and the products you handle remain the property of your clients. This position is unchanged.

The following guidance is provided in response to the specific questions you asked during our call.

**1. If the Singapore enquiry becomes a firm order**

If the exporter of record (the party that owns the goods and is selling them overseas) holds an existing export arrangement, your facility may be added to that arrangement as an approved storage site. The process is initiated by the exporter, not by you. The exporter will need to contact the relevant authority in their own supply chain, which for most processed foods will be the Commonwealth Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF) or this Department under a delegated arrangement.

If your Wingfield site is not already listed on the exporter's registration, the exporter can apply to have it added. Our officers may then need to inspect the facility again to confirm it meets the relevant cold chain requirements for the specific commodity. I note that the inspection in September confirmed that your temperature monitoring systems are operating within the ranges you have documented, and that your corrective action procedures for temperature excursions are adequate. These records will be relevant if an application is made.

**2. If Adelaide Cold Chain Logistics becomes the exporter of record**

If you were to purchase product and sell it overseas in your own name, you would become the exporter and would need to hold the necessary export documentation. You should contact us before committing to any overseas order in that scenario, so we can advise on the specific commodity requirements. Different commodities have different certification requirements, and some require a health certificate issued by this Department or by DAFF.

**3. Food safety registration with council**

You asked whether your existing registration with the City of Port Adelaide Enfield is sufficient. For domestic purposes, yes. The *Food Act 2001* (SA) requires food businesses to be registered with their local council, and a storage facility that does not itself sell food to the public is not required to hold a separate registration with PIRSA. Your council registration covers the handling of the products while they are in your care.
